chapter.name: Panchayati Raj

concepts.name: Evolution of Panchayati Raj: committees up to constitutionalisation

questions.q: The committee appointed in January 1957 to examine the working of the Community Development Programme (1952) and the National Extension Service (1953), and whose report led to the scheme of 'democratic decentralisation', was chaired by
questions.e: p.548: the committee of January 1957 under Balwantrai G. Mehta reported in November 1957 and recommended 'democratic decentralisation', which came to be known as Panchayati Raj.
w: Ashok Mehta headed the Janata Government's committee of December 1977 (p.550).
G.V.K. Rao headed the Planning Commission's 1985 committee on administrative arrangements for rural development (p.551).
L.M. Singhvi headed the 1986 concept-paper committee (p.552).

questions.q: In place of the three-tier structure, the Ashok Mehta Committee (1977-78) recommended
questions.a: a two-tier system of a zila parishad at the district level and, below it, a mandal panchayat for a group of villages
o: a two-tier system of a zila parishad at the district level and, below it, a mandal panchayat for a group of villages
a two-tier system of a panchayat samiti at the block level and a gram panchayat for each village
a single-tier system with the gram panchayat as the only elected body
a four-tier system with a separate judicial tier of nyaya panchayats
questions.e: p.550: the three-tier system was to be replaced by the two-tier system - zila parishad and, below it, the mandal panchayat of 15,000-20,000 population; the district was to be the first point of decentralisation.
w: The committee made the district, not the block, the first point of decentralisation (p.550).
It sought to replace the three-tier system by two tiers, not one (p.550).
The four-tier pattern was West Bengal's own arrangement, not the committee's proposal (p.549).

questions.q: The committee which concluded that the developmental process had been bureaucratised and divorced from Panchayati Raj, so that the institutions were aptly called 'grass without roots', was
questions.a: the G.V.K. Rao Committee, appointed by the Planning Commission in 1985
o: the G.V.K. Rao Committee, appointed by the Planning Commission in 1985
the L.M. Singhvi Committee, appointed by the Rajiv Gandhi government in 1986
the Thungon Committee, a sub-committee of the Consultative Committee of Parliament
the Gadgil Committee, constituted by the Congress party in 1988
questions.e: p.551: the G.V.K. Rao Committee (Planning Commission, 1985) found the bureaucratisation of development weakened the Panchayati Raj institutions, 'grass without roots'.
w: Singhvi's concept paper sought constitutional recognition, not the 'grass without roots' finding (p.552).
Thungon examined the district-level planning structure and recommended constitutional recognition (p.553).
Gadgil's committee considered how best the institutions could be made effective (p.553).

questions.a: Andhra Pradesh adopted the system in 1958, ahead of Rajasthan

The scheme was inaugurated by the prime minister on 2 October 1959 in Nagaur district of Rajasthan
Rajasthan was the first state to establish Panchayati Raj
The National Development Council accepted the committee's recommendations in January 1958
questions.e: p.549: Rajasthan was the first state; Andhra Pradesh, which also adopted the system in 1959, followed it.
w: This is correct (p.549).
This is correct (p.549).
This is correct (p.549).

questions.q: The 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill, introduced by the Rajiv Gandhi Government in July 1989 to constitutionalise Panchayati Raj institutions, did not become law because
questions.a: it was passed by the Lok Sabha in August 1989 but was not approved by the Rajya Sabha
o: it was passed by the Lok Sabha in August 1989 but was not approved by the Rajya Sabha
it lapsed in the Lok Sabha with the fall of the National Front Government in 1990
it was passed by both Houses but the State legislatures refused to ratify it
it was withdrawn after the Planning Commission opposed it
questions.e: p.554: the Lok Sabha passed the bill in August 1989 but the Rajya Sabha did not approve it; the Opposition said it sought to strengthen centralisation in the federal system.
w: The lapse on the fall of a government is what happened to the September 1990 bill, not the 1989 bill (p.554).
The text records that the Rajya Sabha did not approve it; no ratification stage is mentioned (p.554).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Balwantrai Mehta Committee and its follow-up:

1. It recommended that the village panchayat be constituted with directly elected representatives, and the panchayat samiti and zila parishad with indirectly elected members.
2. It recommended that the zila parishad be the executive body and the panchayat samiti the advisory, coordinating and supervisory body.
3. It recommended that the district collector be the chairman of the zila parishad.
4. The National Development Council accepted the recommendations in January 1958 but left the states free to evolve their own patterns.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.548 says gram panchayat members were to be directly elected, the samiti and parishad indirectly. Statement 2 is incorrect: the roles are swapped: the panchayat samiti was to be the executive body and the zila parishad the advisory, coordinating and supervisory body (p.548). Statement 3 is correct: p.548 lists the collector as chairman of the zila parishad. Statement 4 is correct: p.549: the Council left the pattern to the states, though basic principles were to be identical.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.548
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.548
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.548

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the patterns of Panchayati Raj that emerged by the mid-1960s:

1. Tamil Nadu adopted the two-tier system.
2. West Bengal adopted the four-tier system.
3. In the Maharashtra-Gujarat pattern the panchayat samiti was the powerful body because the block was the unit of planning.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.549 gives Tamil Nadu as the two-tier example. Statement 2 is correct: p.549 gives West Bengal as the four-tier example. Statement 3 is incorrect: in the Maharashtra-Gujarat pattern the zila parishad was powerful as the district was the unit; the samiti-centred pattern was Rajasthan-Andhra Pradesh (p.549).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.549
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.549
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.549

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ashok Mehta Committee:

1. It recommended official participation of political parties at all levels of panchayat elections.
2. It recommended that the nyaya panchayats be merged with the development panchayats under a single elected head.
3. It recommended compulsory powers of taxation for the panchayati raj institutions.
4. Its recommendations were implemented at the central level by the Janata Government through a constitutional amendment.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.550 lists participation of political parties at all levels. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.551 says nyaya panchayats were to be kept separate from development panchayats and presided over by a qualified judge. Statement 3 is correct: p.550 lists compulsory powers of taxation. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.551: owing to the collapse of the Janata Government no action was taken at the central level; only Karnataka, West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh took some steps.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.550
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.550
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.550

Consider the following statements:

1. The G.V.K. Rao Committee recommended a post of District Development Commissioner as chief executive officer of the Zila Parishad.
2. The G.V.K. Rao Committee found that elections had become overdue for one or more tiers in 11 states.
3. The Hanumantha Rao Committee (1984) recommended that the Collector should be the coordinator of all developmental and planning activities at the district level.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements about the L.M. Singhvi Committee:

1. It recommended that a new chapter be added to the Constitution to recognise and protect Panchayati Raj institutions.
2. It recommended that nyaya panchayats be established in every village so that each gram panchayat has its own court.
3. It described the Gram Sabha as the embodiment of direct democracy.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.552: a new chapter in the Constitution was proposed. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.552: nyaya panchayats were to be established for a cluster of villages, not for each village. Statement 3 is correct: p.552 calls the Gram Sabha the embodiment of direct democracy.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.552
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.552
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.552

concepts.description: Committees and bills on Panchayati Raj from 1957 to 1991.
concepts.idea: Panchayati Raj grew through successive committees until the 73rd Amendment gave it constitutional status.
concepts.rule: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee (reported November 1957) recommended a three-tier system; Rajasthan began it on 2 October 1959 at Nagaur, followed by Andhra Pradesh. The Ashok Mehta Committee (1978) proposed a two-tier system with a mandal panchayat. The G.V.K. Rao Committee called the result 'grass without roots'. The Singhvi, Thungon and Gadgil committees urged constitutional recognition. The 64th Amendment Bill passed the Lok Sabha in 1989 but not the Rajya Sabha. The Narasimha Rao Government's 1991 bill became the 73rd Amendment, in force from 24 April 1993 (pp.548-554).
concepts.example: Ashok Mehta Committee: zila parishad and mandal panchayat of 15,000-20,000 people.

concepts.name: The 73rd Amendment Act: Part IX, structure, compulsory and voluntary provisions

questions.q: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 added to the Constitution a new Part IX, entitled 'The Panchayats', consisting of
questions.e: p.554: Part IX consists of provisions from Articles 243 to 243-O; Table 39.2 starts with Article 243 (Definitions) and ends with 243-O.
w: Articles 243-K to 243-O (elections, Union territories, exempted areas, continuance of laws, bar to court interference) are also in Part IX (p.566).
Article 243 itself, the definitions article, is part of Part IX (p.565).
The Part runs beyond Article 243-G, which deals with powers, authority and responsibilities (p.566).

questions.q: Which one of the following is a compulsory (obligatory) provision of Part IX that the states must include in their panchayat laws?
questions.a: Voting rights for the chairperson and other members of a panchayat, whether elected directly or indirectly
o: Voting rights for the chairperson and other members of a panchayat, whether elected directly or indirectly
Reservation of seats for backward classes in panchayats at any level
Representation of members of Parliament and the state legislature in panchayats within their constituencies
Authorising panchayats to levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls and fees
questions.e: p.559: the compulsory list includes voting rights of the chairperson and members elected directly or indirectly; p.560 lists the other three as voluntary.
w: Reservation for backward classes is a voluntary provision (p.560).
Representation of MPs and MLAs is a voluntary provision (p.560).
Granting financial powers is a voluntary provision (p.560).

questions.q: The 73rd Amendment Act does not apply to the states of
questions.e: p.557: the Act does not apply to Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram and certain other areas.
w: Manipur is not exempted as a whole; only its hill areas with district councils are (p.557).
Tripura is not named among the exempted states (p.557).
Assam is not named; only some tribal areas in it fall outside (p.557, p.567).

questions.q: A state having a population not exceeding which of the following may choose not to constitute panchayats at the intermediate level?
questions.e: p.555: the three-tier system is uniform, but a state with a population not exceeding 20 lakh may not constitute panchayats at the intermediate level.
w: The limit is 20 lakh, not 10 lakh (p.555).
The limit is 20 lakh, not 25 lakh (p.555).
The limit is 20 lakh, not 50 lakh (p.555).

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct about the election of members and chairpersons of panchayats under the Act?
questions.a: The chairperson of a panchayat at the intermediate and district levels is elected directly by the people
o: The chairperson of a panchayat at the intermediate and district levels is elected directly by the people
The chairperson of a panchayat at the village level is elected in the manner the state legislature determines
The chairperson of a panchayat at the intermediate level is elected by and from amongst its elected members
The chairperson and the other members of a panchayat have the right to vote in its meetings
questions.e: p.555: chairpersons at the intermediate and district levels are elected indirectly, by and from amongst the elected members; all members are directly elected.
w: This is correct (p.555).
This is correct (p.555).
This is correct (p.555).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Gram Sabha under the 73rd Amendment:

1. The Gram Sabha consists of the elected members of the village panchayat.
2. The Gram Sabha may exercise such powers and perform such functions as the state legislature determines.
3. Endowing the Gram Sabha with powers and functions at the village level is a compulsory provision of the Act.
4. Organisation of the Gram Sabha in a village or group of villages is a compulsory provision of the Act.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.555: it consists of all persons registered in the electoral rolls of the village, not only elected members. Statement 2 is correct: p.555. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.560 lists endowing the Gram Sabha with powers as voluntary. Statement 4 is correct: p.559 lists organisation of the Gram Sabha as compulsory.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.555
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.555
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.555

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the structure of panchayats:

1. The Act provides a three-tier system, with panchayats at the village, intermediate and district levels, in every state.
2. A state having a population not exceeding 20 lakh need not constitute panchayats at the intermediate level.
3. The Act leaves the formation of panchayats and the holding of elections at regular intervals dependent on the will of the state government.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.555. Statement 2 is correct: p.555. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.554-555: neither formation of panchayats nor regular elections depends on the will of the state government any more.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.555
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.555
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.555

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the election of members and chairpersons under the Act:

1. All the members of panchayats at the village, intermediate and district levels are elected directly by the people.
2. The chairpersons of panchayats at the intermediate and district levels are also elected directly by the people.
3. The chairperson of a village panchayat is elected in such manner as the state legislature determines.
4. A chairperson elected indirectly has no right to vote in meetings of the panchayat.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.555. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.555: they are elected indirectly, by and from amongst the elected members. Statement 3 is correct: p.555. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.555: the chairperson and other members, directly or indirectly elected, have the right to vote.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.555

questions.q:
Which of the following are voluntary (discretionary) provisions of Part IX?

1. Giving representation to members of Parliament and the state legislature in panchayats within their constituencies.
2. Providing for grants-in-aid to the panchayats from the consolidated fund of the state.
3. Giving representation to the chairpersons of the intermediate panchayats in the district panchayats.
4. Establishing a State Election Commission to conduct panchayat elections.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.560 voluntary item 5. Statement 2 is correct: p.560 voluntary item 11. Statement 3 is correct: p.560 voluntary item 4. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.560 lists the State Election Commission among compulsory provisions (item 10).
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.560
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.560
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.560

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the exemptions from Part IX:

1. The Darjeeling district of West Bengal, for which the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council exists, is exempted.
2. The whole of Manipur is exempted, since its hill areas have district councils.
3. Parliament has no power to extend Part IX to the scheduled areas and tribal areas.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.557. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.557: only the hill areas of Manipur for which district councils exist are exempted. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.557: Parliament may extend the Part with exceptions and modifications; the PESA Act of 1996 is an example (p.558).
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.557
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.557
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.557

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about continuance of laws and interference by courts:

concepts.description: Structure and compulsory/voluntary provisions of Part IX.
concepts.idea: The 73rd Amendment added Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) and made a three-tier panchayat system obligatory on states.
concepts.rule: Part IX covers Articles 243 to 243-O and gives practical shape to Article 40. The Gram Sabha is the foundation and there are three tiers, though a state with up to 20 lakh people may skip the intermediate tier. Compulsory provisions include organising the Gram Sabha, three tiers, direct election of all members, voting rights, a five-year term, a State Election Commission and a State Finance Commission. Voluntary provisions include the manner of electing the village chairperson, backward-class reservation, taxation powers and devolution of the Eleventh Schedule functions. Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram and certain other areas are exempted, and courts cannot interfere in panchayat electoral matters (pp.554-560, 565-566).
concepts.example: The village chairperson is elected as the state legislature decides, a voluntary matter.

concepts.description: Powers, Eleventh Schedule, finances, State Finance Commission and audit.
concepts.idea: The state legislature devolves powers and finances to panchayats, with the 29 Eleventh Schedule matters as a guide.
concepts.rule: The state legislature may endow panchayats with self-government powers, including plans and schemes on the 29 Eleventh Schedule matters. It may authorise taxes, assign state taxes, give grants-in-aid from the state consolidated fund and create funds. The governor constitutes a State Finance Commission every five years and places its recommendations, with an action taken report, before the state legislature; the legislature of the state may provide for the commission's composition. The Central Finance Commission suggests measures to supplement panchayat resources. Audit is left to the state legislature (pp.554, 556-559, 566).
concepts.example: Fisheries is item 5 and libraries item 20 of the Eleventh Schedule.

concepts.description: PESA Act 1996 for the Fifth Schedule areas.
concepts.idea: Parliament extended Part IX to Scheduled Areas through PESA with the Gram Sabha as the nucleus.
concepts.rule: Part IX does not apply to Fifth Schedule areas unless Parliament extends it; PESA (1996) does so for ten states. The Gram Sabha approves plans, and the village panchayat must obtain from it a certification of utilisation of funds. Tribal reservation is not less than one-half of seats and all chairperson seats are reserved for STs; nominations are capped at one-tenth. The Gram Sabha's recommendation is mandatory for minor-mineral licences and leases. Panchayats get ownership of minor forest produce and control over intoxicants, land alienation and money lending (pp.560-563).
concepts.example: Land acquisition: the Gram Sabha is consulted, projects are coordinated at state level.

concepts.idea: Panchayats remain dependent on tied grants and weak devolution despite constitutional status.
